deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). π is the (profinite) fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. It has inertia generators l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1, and L_i is the inertia subgroup generated by l_i. Grothendieck works with an extension S\hat{\hat E} of \hat{\hat Γ} (exterior automorphisms) whose elements are 5-tuples (p, σ, g_0, g_1, g_∞). Here p ∈ \hat Z^* is the exponent, σ ∈ S_3 permutes the cusps, and the g_i ∈ π are 'rectificateurs'. The tuple encodes the automorphism l_i ↦ g_i l_{σ(i)}^p g_i^{-1}. For this to be an automorphism of π, the defining relation must be preserved. S E is the discrete-exponent part, p ∈ Z^* = {±1}.

On this page Grothendieck studies the subset of tuples with g_0 = g_1 = g_∞ = 1. This subset is a subgroup (evident from formula (8)). The tuple (p, σ, 1, 1, 1) is admissible iff (13) holds: l_{σ(0)}^p l_{σ(1)}^p l_{σ(∞)}^p = 1.

Case p ∈ {±1}.
- p = 1: the relation holds exactly for the cyclic rotations of the relation, i.e. σ even.
- p = -1: l_a^{-1} l_b^{-1} l_c^{-1} = (l_c l_b l_a)^{-1}, so the relation holds exactly for σ reversing the cyclic order, i.e. σ odd.
- Hence (p, σ) satisfies (13) iff p = sg(σ), i.e. (σ, p) ∈ Γ_p = {(σ, sg σ)} ≅ S_3.

Conclusion. The lifted group \tilde Γ_p ⊂ S E (the image of the canonical section (11)-(12) from the previous page) is characterized as the group of automorphisms of π that preserve L_0, L_1, L_∞ with all rectifiers trivial.

Conjecture and exercise. He conjectures the same holds in S\hat{\hat E}: (13) with p ∈ \hat Z^* forces p = ±1. After composing with an element of \tilde Γ_p one may assume σ = id. The claim then reduces to an exercise: x^p y^p = (xy)^p in the free profinite group on x = l_0, y = l_1 forces p = 1.

The exercise is true.
- Map to the Heisenberg group mod ℓ^k (ℓ odd). There (xy)^p = x^p y^p [y,x]^{p(p-1)/2}, which forces p ≡ 1 mod ℓ^k.
- A similar argument with nonabelian 2-groups (e.g. dihedral groups) handles ℓ = 2.
- So p = 1 in \hat Z.

This is the same computation as showing that (λ, f = 1) ∈ \hat{GT} forces λ = 1, since relation (II) with f = 1 reads z^m y^m x^m = 1.
errors: Relation (14) is written l_∞^p l_1^p l_0^p = 1 with the claim that it implies p = 1. With the convention l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1 used in (13) for σ = id, p = -1 actually satisfies (14), because l_∞^{-1} l_1^{-1} l_0^{-1} = (l_0 l_1 l_∞)^{-1} = 1. After normalizing σ = id the intended relation should be l_0^p l_1^p l_∞^p = 1. Alternatively, with the reversed order, the conclusion should be p = -1. This is a minor slip in ordering or sign.
The conjecture 'sans doute' (that (13) forces p ∈ {±1} in the profinite setting) is correct. It is left as an exercise, with no argument given.

ideas.what: Automorphisms of the profinite π_1 of P^1-{0,1,∞} that send each inertia generator l_i to l_{σ(i)}^p with trivial conjugating elements form exactly S_3, embedded via σ ↦ (σ, sg σ).
ideas.modern_name: S_3 symmetry of P^1-{0,1,∞} inside the Grothendieck–Teichmüller / inertia-preserving outer automorphism group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; implicit in Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara's work on \hat{GT} and Out^♯(\hat F_2)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'Teichmüller tower' and Gal action, but not this explicit computation

ideas.what: Exercise: x^λ y^λ = (xy)^λ in the free profinite group \hat F_2 with λ ∈ \hat Z^* implies λ = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Power maps are endomorphisms only for trivial exponent; equivalently (λ, 1) ∈ \hat{GT} iff λ = 1

ideas.what: Encoding automorphisms by (p, σ, g_0, g_1, g_∞) with 'rectificateurs' g_i, and a partial section of S E over Γ.
ideas.modern_name: Description of \hat{GT}-type groups via (λ, f) pairs / inertia-preserving automorphisms with conjugators

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification within Grothendieck's 1981 anabelian/Galois–Teichmüller computations. It identifies the trivially-rectified part of S E with S_3 ≅ Γ_p and poses an easy exercise. Nothing here goes beyond standard facts later made explicit by Drinfeld and Ihara.
transcription_corrections: 'Quand on a borne' should read 'Quand on se borne à S E au lieu de S\hat{\hat E}'.
'mieux encore[?] que' is more likely 'vu encore que' or 'notant que'. The reading is uncertain; the sense is 'noting that {±1}×S_3 ≅ S_3×Z_2 ≅ Γ'.
'dans S\hat{\hat{\mathcal E}}_i,' should read 'dans S\hat{\hat{\mathcal E}},'. The apparent subscript is the comma.
'Je reviens au [?] du dire]' should read 'Je reviens au même de dire', i.e. 'cela revient au même de dire'.
In the insertion, read '(quitte à corriger par un \tilde σ_i ou σ ∈ Γ_p)'.
